[classes]
# The closed list of classes of work (D42). Adding a class is a job.
list = ["code", "tests", "docs", "prompts", "config", "build", "design", "other"]

[forecast.reference]
# The reference forecaster's priors, used until history accumulates (design §9.2).

wall_time_s = { p10 = 120.0, p50 = 420.0, p90 = 1500.0 }

[secrets]
# Reviewed gitleaks allow-list entries, each with a reason. Commit an entry before the commit it excuses.
allowlist = []

[tools.gitleaks]
version = "8.30.1"
sha256 = { linux_x64 = "551f6fc83ea457d62a0d98237cbad105af8d557003051f41f3e7ca7b3f2470eb", linux_arm64 = "e4a487ee7ccd7d3a7f7ec08657610aa3606637dab924210b3aee62570fb4b080", darwin_x64 = "dfe101a4db2255fc85120ac7f3d25e4342c3c20cf749f2c20a18081af1952709", darwin_arm64 = "b40ab0ae55c505963e365f271a8d3846efbc170aa17f2607f13df610a9aeb6a5" }

[history]
# Commits that predate Athena and are exempt from the governed-content invariant (design §7.3). Each entry is
# a full commit id, and a commit that adds one must already have that commit in its history (D60).
# 64ecdc9 is a parentless second root that Athena's own commit path wrote during job 20261010-132713-ezm8;
# it joined main through the merge of the bootstrap (361a786) and fails the records-based landing check.
# ee4b0dd1aa6fcd81289dc988d0f7bd38fd7a40ef is the squash of PR #8, which carried several jobs' landings in one
# commit; the landing check refuses that shape. Excused by the user's choice of option (a) in D66: this one
# commit's content skips the invariant, and its jobs' own records still get the per-record checks.
# f2a8453380196b95f2e2cc629ffa969af57e6c85 is the squash of PR #9. Most of that PR's jobs predate
# athena.candidate/2, so the chain landing rule (D69) cannot link them (D70).
# 5a734782e76daac9b12bd8833c97a73927c8cf94 is the squash of PR #14. It changes records/ but names no job,
# so the per-job records check cannot tie its content to a job (D76).
exempt = ["49c6ac1524677b8091081115fb5d410ed6d2b2ea", "64ecdc9aa4fd24cbe4d4884c864d7e9041585c3d", "ee4b0dd1aa6fcd81289dc988d0f7bd38fd7a40ef", "f2a8453380196b95f2e2cc629ffa969af57e6c85", "5a734782e76daac9b12bd8833c97a73927c8cf94"]

[records]
max_file_bytes = 1048576

[personal_data]
# Email addresses allowed in committed content. An entry ending in "@" allows that local part ("noreply@");
# one starting with "@" allows that domain; one starting with "." allows every domain under that suffix.
# These are no-reply addresses, the documentation domains, and the reserved top-level domains (RFC 2606),
# none of which can belong to a person.
email_allow = ["noreply@", "@example.com", "@example.org", "@example.net", ".invalid", ".test", ".example"]

# Athena asks the host to merge a pull request once its checks are green, so `athena land --pr` finishes
# the landing without a manual merge step. Red or pending checks never trigger a merge.
[landing]
merge_via_rest = true

# How many jobs `athena drain` runs at once: the independent items of one plan group (no dependency, disjoint
# touched paths). 1 is one job at a time, as before; the schema allows 1 to 8. Left at 1 here, so adding the
# section changes nothing until the user raises it.
[parallel]
max_concurrency = 1
